subtopic: Integration as the Inverse of Differentiation
stem: Write an anti derivative for each of the following functions using the method of inspection: (i) \(\cos 2x\)  (ii) \(3x^2 + 4x^3\)  (iii) \(\dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x \neq 0\).
solution:
(i) We look for a function whose derivative is \(\cos 2x\). Since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin 2x = 2\cos 2x\), we have \(\cos 2x = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin 2x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)\). Therefore an anti derivative of \(\cos 2x\) is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\).
(ii) Note that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^3 + x^4\right) = 3x^2 + 4x^3\). Therefore an anti derivative of \(3x^2 + 4x^3\) is \(x^3 + x^4\).
(iii) We know that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x > 0\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[\log(-x)] = \dfrac{1}{-x}(-1) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x < 0\). Combining these, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log|x|\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x \neq 0\). Therefore \(\int \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \log|x|\) is one of the anti derivatives of \(\dfrac{1}{x}\).

subtopic: Integration as the Inverse of Differentiation
stem: Find the following integrals: (i) \(\int \dfrac{x^3 - 1}{x^2}\,dx\)  (ii) \(\int \left(x^{2/3} + 1\right) dx\)  (iii) \(\int \left(x^{3/2} + 2e^x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx\).
solution:
(i) \(\int \dfrac{x^3 - 1}{x^2}\,dx = \int x\,dx - \int x^{-2}\,dx\) (by Property V) \(= \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^{-1}}{-1} + C = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{1}{x} + C\), where \(C\) is a constant of integration.
(ii) \(\int \left(x^{2/3} + 1\right) dx = \int x^{2/3}\,dx + \int dx = \dfrac{x^{2/3 + 1}}{\tfrac{2}{3} + 1} + x + C = \dfrac{3}{5}x^{5/3} + x + C\).
(iii) \(\int \left(x^{3/2} + 2e^x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx = \int x^{3/2}\,dx + \int 2e^x\,dx - \int \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \dfrac{x^{3/2 + 1}}{\tfrac{3}{2} + 1} + 2e^x - \log|x| + C = \dfrac{2}{5}x^{5/2} + 2e^x - \log|x| + C\).

subtopic: Integration as the Inverse of Differentiation
stem: Find the following integrals: (i) \(\int (\sin x + \cos x)\,dx\)  (ii) \(\int \csc x\,(\csc x + \cot x)\,dx\)  (iii) \(\int \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx\).
solution:
(i) \(\int (\sin x + \cos x)\,dx = \int \sin x\,dx + \int \cos x\,dx = -\cos x + \sin x + C\).
(ii) \(\int \csc x\,(\csc x + \cot x)\,dx = \int \csc^2 x\,dx + \int \csc x \cot x\,dx = -\cot x - \csc x + C\).
(iii) \(\int \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx = \int \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x}\,dx - \int \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx = \int \sec^2 x\,dx - \int \tan x \sec x\,dx = \tan x - \sec x + C\).

subtopic: Integration as the Inverse of Differentiation
stem: Find the anti derivative \(F\) of \(f\) defined by \(f(x) = 4x^3 - 6\), where \(F(0) = 3\).
solution: One anti derivative of \(f(x)\) is \(x^4 - 6x\), since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^4 - 6x\right) = 4x^3 - 6\). Therefore the anti derivative \(F\) is given by \(F(x) = x^4 - 6x + C\), where \(C\) is a constant. Given \(F(0) = 3\), which gives \(3 = 0 - 6 \times 0 + C\), or \(C = 3\). Hence the required anti derivative is the unique function \(F\) defined by \(F(x) = x^4 - 6x + 3\).

solution: We observe that \(\sin^2 x\) is an even function. Therefore, by \(P_7\)(i), we get \(\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4} \sin^2 x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \sin^2 x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/4}(1 - \cos 2x)\,dx = \left[x - \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right]_{0}^{\pi/4} = \left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{2}\sin \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 0 = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{2}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx\). Then, by \(P_4\), we have \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{(\pi - x)\sin(\pi - x)}{1 + \cos^2(\pi - x)}\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{(\pi - x)\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx - I\). Or \(2I = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx\), or \(I = \frac{\pi}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx\). Put \(\cos x = t\) so that \(-\sin x\,dx = dt\). When \(x = 0\), \(t = 1\) and when \(x = \pi\), \(t = -1\). Therefore, (by \(P_1\)) we get \(I = \frac{-\pi}{2}\int_{1}^{-1} \frac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \frac{\pi}{2}\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \pi\int_{0}^{1} \frac{dt}{1 + t^2}\) (by \(P_7\), since \(\frac{1}{1+t^2}\) is even function) \(= \pi\left[\tan^{-1} t\right]_{0}^{1} = \pi\left[\tan^{-1} 1 - \tan^{-1} 0\right] = \pi\left[\frac{\pi}{4} - 0\right] = \frac{\pi^2}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{-1}^{1} \sin^5 x \cos^4 x\,dx\). Let \(f(x) = \sin^5 x \cos^4 x\). Then \(f(-x) = \sin^5(-x)\cos^4(-x) = -\sin^5 x \cos^4 x = -f(x)\), i.e., \(f\) is an odd function. Therefore, by \(P_7\)(ii), \(I = 0\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^4 x}{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x}\,dx\) ... (1). Then, by \(P_4\), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^4\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}{\sin^4\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right) + \cos^4\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos^4 x}{\cos^4 x + \sin^4 x}\,dx\) ... (2). Adding (1) and (2), we get \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x}{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x}\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} dx = [x]_{0}^{\pi/2} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Hence \(I = \frac{\pi}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}} = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos x}\,dx}{\sqrt{\cos x} + \sqrt{\sin x}}\) ... (1). Then, by \(P_3\) (with \(a + b = \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}\)), \(I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{6} - x\right)}}{\sqrt{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{6} - x\right)} + \sqrt{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{6} - x\right)}}\,dx = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x} + \sqrt{\cos x}}\,dx\) ... (2). Adding (1) and (2), we get \(2I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} dx = [x]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} = \frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Hence \(I = \frac{\pi}{12}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin x\,dx\). Then, by \(P_4\), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \cos x\,dx\). Adding the two values of I, we get \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\log \sin x + \log \cos x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\log \sin x \cos x + \log 2 - \log 2)\,dx\) (by adding and subtracting \(\log 2\)) \(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin 2x\,dx - \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log 2\,dx\). Put \(2x = t\) in the first integral. Then \(2\,dx = dt\), when \(x = 0\), \(t = 0\) and when \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(t = \pi\). Therefore \(2I = \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi} \log \sin t\,dt - \frac{\pi}{2}\log 2 = \frac{2}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin t\,dt - \frac{\pi}{2}\log 2\) (by \(P_6\) as \(\sin(\pi - t) = \sin t\)) \(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin x\,dx - \frac{\pi}{2}\log 2\) (by changing variable \(t\) to \(x\)) \(= I - \frac{\pi}{2}\log 2\). Hence \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \log \sin x\,dx = \frac{-\pi}{2}\log 2\).

solution: We know that derivative of \(mx\) is \(m\). Thus, we make the substitution \(mx = t\) so that \(m\,dx = dt\). Therefore, \(\int \sin mx\,dx = \frac{1}{m}\int \sin t\,dt = -\frac{1}{m}\cos t + C = -\frac{1}{m}\cos mx + C\).

Derivative of \(x^2 + 1\) is \(2x\). Thus, we use the substitution \(x^2 + 1 = t\) so that \(2x\,dx = dt\). Therefore, \(\int 2x \sin (x^2 + 1)\,dx = \int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t + C = -\cos (x^2 + 1) + C\).

Derivative of \(\sqrt{x}\) is \(\frac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\). Thus, we use the substitution \(\sqrt{x} = t\) so that \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx = dt\) giving \(dx = 2t\,dt\). Thus, \(\int \frac{\tan^4 \sqrt{x}\, \sec^2 \sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx = \int \frac{2t \tan^4 t\, \sec^2 t\,dt}{t} = 2\int \tan^4 t\, \sec^2 t\,dt\). Again, we make another substitution \(\tan t = u\) so that \(\sec^2 t\,dt = du\). Therefore, \(2\int \tan^4 t\, \sec^2 t\,dt = 2\int u^4\,du = 2\frac{u^5}{5} + C = \frac{2}{5}\tan^5 t + C\) (since \(u = \tan t\)) \(= \frac{2}{5}\tan^5 \sqrt{x} + C\) (since \(t = \sqrt{x}\)). Hence, \(\int \frac{\tan^4 \sqrt{x}\, \sec^2 \sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx = \frac{2}{5}\tan^5 \sqrt{x} + C\).

Derivative of \(\tan^{-1} x\) is \(\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\). Thus, we use the substitution \(\tan^{-1} x = t\) so that \(\frac{dx}{1 + x^2} = dt\). Therefore, \(\int \frac{\sin (\tan^{-1} x)}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t + C = -\cos (\tan^{-1} x) + C\).

We have \(\int \sin^3 x \cos^2 x\,dx = \int \sin^2 x \cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx = \int (1 - \cos^2 x)\cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx\). Put \(t = \cos x\) so that \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Therefore, \(\int \sin^2 x \cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx = -\int (1 - t^2) t^2\,dt = -\int (t^2 - t^4)\,dt = -\left(\frac{t^3}{3} - \frac{t^5}{5}\right) + C = -\frac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + \frac{1}{5}\cos^5 x + C\).

Put \(x + a = t\). Then \(dx = dt\). Therefore, \(\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin (x + a)}\,dx = \int \frac{\sin (t - a)}{\sin t}\,dt = \int \frac{\sin t \cos a - \cos t \sin a}{\sin t}\,dt = \cos a \int dt - \sin a \int \cot t\,dt = (\cos a)\,t - (\sin a)\left[\log |\sin t| + C_1\right] = (\cos a)(x + a) - (\sin a)\left[\log |\sin (x + a)| + C_1\right] = x \cos a + a \cos a - (\sin a)\log |\sin (x + a)| - C_1 \sin a\). Hence, \(\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin (x + a)}\,dx = x \cos a - \sin a \log |\sin (x + a)| + C\), where \(C = -C_1 \sin a + a \cos a\), is another arbitrary constant.

\(\int \frac{dx}{1 + \tan x} = \int \frac{\cos x\,dx}{\cos x + \sin x} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{(\cos x + \sin x + \cos x - \sin x)\,dx}{\cos x + \sin x} = \frac{1}{2}\int dx + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{C_1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx\) ...(1). Now, consider \(I = \int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx\). Put \(\cos x + \sin x = t\) so that \((\cos x - \sin x)\,dx = dt\). Therefore \(I = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log |t| + C_2 = \log |\cos x + \sin x| + C_2\). Putting it in (1), we get \(\int \frac{dx}{1 + \tan x} = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\log |\cos x + \sin x| + C\), where \(C = \frac{C_1}{2} + \frac{C_2}{2}\).

solution: Recall the identity \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\), which gives \(\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\). Therefore \(\int \cos^2 x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int (1+\cos 2x)\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int dx + \dfrac{1}{2}\int \cos 2x\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}\sin 2x + C\).

Recall the identity \(\sin x \cos y = \dfrac{1}{2}[\sin (x+y) + \sin (x-y)]\). Then \(\int \sin 2x \cos 3x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\int \sin 5x\,dx - \int \sin x\,dx\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[-\dfrac{1}{5}\cos 5x + \cos x\right] + C = -\dfrac{1}{10}\cos 5x + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x + C\).

From the identity \(\sin 3x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x\), we find that \(\sin^3 x = \dfrac{3\sin x - \sin 3x}{4}\). Therefore \(\int \sin^3 x\,dx = \dfrac{3}{4}\int \sin x\,dx - \dfrac{1}{4}\int \sin 3x\,dx = -\dfrac{3}{4}\cos x + \dfrac{1}{12}\cos 3x + C\). Alternatively, \(\int \sin^3 x\,dx = \int (1-\cos^2 x)\sin x\,dx\); putting \(\cos x = t\) so that \(-\sin x\,dx = dt\) gives \(-\int (1-t^2)\,dt = -t + \dfrac{t^3}{3} + C = -\cos x + \dfrac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + C\). Both answers are equivalent.

solution:
(i) \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-16} = \int \frac{dx}{x^2-4^2} = \frac{1}{8}\log\left|\frac{x-4}{x+4}\right| + C\) [by 7.4(1)].
(ii) \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{2x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}}\). Put \(x-1=t\), so \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{2x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}(t) + C\) [by 7.4(5)] \(= \sin^{-1}(x-1) + C\).

(i) We have \(x^2-6x+13 = x^2-6x+3^2-3^2+13 = (x-3)^2+4\). So \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-6x+13} = \int \frac{1}{(x-3)^2+2^2}\,dx\). Let \(x-3=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-6x+13} = \int \frac{dt}{t^2+2^2} = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{2} + C\) [by 7.4(3)] \(= \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x-3}{2} + C\).
(ii) The given integral is of the form 7.4(7). We write \(3x^2+13x-10 = 3\left(x^2+\frac{13x}{3}-\frac{10}{3}\right) = 3\left[\left(x+\frac{13}{6}\right)^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2\right]\) (completing the square). Thus \(\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+13x-10} = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dx}{\left(x+\frac{13}{6}\right)^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2}\). Put \(x+\frac{13}{6}=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+13x-10} = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{3\times 2\times \frac{17}{6}}\log\left|\frac{t-\frac{17}{6}}{t+\frac{17}{6}}\right| + C_1\) [by 7.4(1)] \(= \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{x+\frac{13}{6}-\frac{17}{6}}{x+\frac{13}{6}+\frac{17}{6}}\right| + C_1 = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{6x-4}{6x+30}\right| + C_1 = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{3x-2}{x+5}\right| + C_1 + \frac{1}{17}\log\frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{3x-2}{x+5}\right| + C\), where \(C = C_1 + \frac{1}{17}\log\frac{1}{3}\).
(iii) We have \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5x^2-2x}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5\left(x^2-\frac{2x}{5}\right)}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{\left(x-\frac{1}{5}\right)^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}}\) (completing the square). Put \(x-\frac{1}{5}=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5x^2-2x}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}\right| + C\) [by 7.4(4)] \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\log\left|x-\frac{1}{5}+\sqrt{x^2-\frac{2x}{5}}\right| + C\).

(i) Using the formula 7.4(9), we express \(x+2 = A\frac{d}{dx}(2x^2+6x+5) + B = A(4x+6) + B\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant terms, \(4A=1\) and \(6A+B=2\), so \(A=\frac{1}{4}\) and \(B=\frac{1}{2}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x+2}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{4x+6}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{2x^2+6x+5} = \frac{1}{4}I_1 + \frac{1}{2}I_2\) ...(1). In \(I_1\), put \(2x^2+6x+5=t\), so \((4x+6)\,dx=dt\); thus \(I_1 = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C_1 = \log|2x^2+6x+5| + C_1\) ...(2). And \(I_2 = \int \frac{dx}{2x^2+6x+5} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+3x+\frac{5}{2}} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}\). Put \(x+\frac{3}{2}=t\), so \(dx=dt\): \(I_2 = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t^2+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{2\times \frac{1}{2}}\tan^{-1}2t + C_2\) [by 7.4(3)] \(= \tan^{-1}2\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right) + C_2 = \tan^{-1}(2x+3) + C_2\) ...(3). Using (2) and (3) in (1): \(\int \frac{x+2}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\log|2x^2+6x+5| + \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2x+3) + C\), where \(C = \frac{C_1}{4} + \frac{C_2}{2}\).
(ii) This integral is of the form given in 7.4(10). Express \(x+3 = A\frac{d}{dx}(5-4x-x^2) + B = A(-4-2x) + B\). Equating coefficients: \(-2A=1\) and \(-4A+B=3\), i.e. \(A=-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(B=1\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x+3}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}}\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{(-4-2x)\,dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} + \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} = -\frac{1}{2}I_1 + I_2\) ...(1). In \(I_1\), put \(5-4x-x^2=t\), so \((-4-2x)\,dx=dt\); thus \(I_1 = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = 2\sqrt{t} + C_1 = 2\sqrt{5-4x-x^2} + C_1\) ...(2). Now \(I_2 = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{9-(x+2)^2}}\). Put \(x+2=t\), so \(dx=dt\): \(I_2 = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{3^2-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{t}{3} + C_2\) [by 7.4(5)] \(= \sin^{-1}\frac{x+2}{3} + C_2\) ...(3). Substituting (2) and (3) in (1): \(\int \frac{x+3}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{5-4x-x^2} + \sin^{-1}\frac{x+2}{3} + C\), where \(C = C_2 - \frac{C_1}{2}\).

The integrand is a proper rational function. By the form of partial fraction [Table 7.2 (i)], write \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{x+2}\). This gives \(1 = A(x+2) + B(x+1)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant term, \(A+B=0\) and \(2A+B=1\), so \(A=1\) and \(B=-1\). Thus \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{1}{x+1} - \frac{1}{x+2}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \int \frac{dx}{x+2} = \log|x+1| - \log|x+2| + C = \log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+2}\right| + C\).

Here the integrand \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\) is not a proper rational function, so we divide \(x^2+1\) by \(x^2-5x+6\) and find that \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)}\). Let \(\frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)} = \frac{A}{x-2} + \frac{B}{x-3}\), so that \(5x-5 = A(x-3) + B(x-2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and constant terms, \(A+B=5\) and \(3A+2B=5\), giving \(A=-5\) and \(B=10\). Thus \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 - \frac{5}{x-2} + \frac{10}{x-3}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\,dx = \int dx - 5\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,dx + 10\int \frac{dx}{x-3} = x - 5\log|x-2| + 10\log|x-3| + C\).

The integrand is of the type as given in Table 7.2 (4). Write \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{(x+1)^2} + \frac{C}{x+3}\), so that \(3x-2 = A(x+1)(x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x+1)^2 = A(x^2+4x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x^2+2x+1)\). Comparing the coefficient of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term on both sides, \(A+C=0\), \(4A+B+2C=3\) and \(3A+3B+C=-2\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{11}{4}\), \(B=\frac{-5}{2}\) and \(C=\frac{-11}{4}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{11}{4(x+1)} - \frac{5}{2(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4(x+3)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)}\,dx = \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \frac{5}{2}\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+3} = \frac{11}{4}\log|x+1| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} - \frac{11}{4}\log|x+3| + C = \frac{11}{4}\log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+3}\right| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} + C\).

Consider \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)}\) and put \(x^2=y\). Then \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = \frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)}\). Write \(\frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)} = \frac{A}{y+1} + \frac{B}{y+4}\), so that \(y = A(y+4) + B(y+1)\). Comparing coefficients of \(y\) and constant terms, \(A+B=1\) and \(4A+B=0\), which give \(A=-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(B=\frac{4}{3}\). Thus \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3(x^2+1)} + \frac{4}{3(x^2+4)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2\,dx}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+1} + \frac{4}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+4} = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{4}{3}\times\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{2}{3}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C\). Here the substitution was made only for the partial fraction part and not for the integration part.

Let \(y=\sin\phi\). Then \(dy=\cos\phi\,d\phi\). Therefore \(\int \frac{(3\sin\phi-2)\cos\phi}{5-\cos^2\phi-4\sin\phi}\,d\phi = \int \frac{(3y-2)\,dy}{5-(1-y^2)-4y} = \int \frac{3y-2}{y^2-4y+4}\,dy = \int \frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2}\,dy = I\) (say). Now write \(\frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2} = \frac{A}{y-2} + \frac{B}{(y-2)^2}\) [by Table 7.2 (2)], so that \(3y-2 = A(y-2) + B\). Comparing the coefficients of \(y\) and constant term, \(A=3\) and \(B-2A=-2\), which give \(A=3\) and \(B=4\). Therefore \(I = \int \left[\frac{3}{y-2} + \frac{4}{(y-2)^2}\right]dy = 3\int \frac{dy}{y-2} + 4\int \frac{dy}{(y-2)^2} = 3\log|y-2| + 4\left(-\frac{1}{y-2}\right) + C = 3\log|\sin\phi-2| + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C = 3\log(2-\sin\phi) + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C\) (since \(2-\sin\phi\) is always positive).

The integrand is a proper rational function. Decompose it into partial fractions [Table 7.2 (5)]. Write \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+2} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}\). Therefore \(x^2+x+1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x+2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term of both sides, \(A+B=1\), \(2B+C=1\) and \(A+2C=1\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{3}{5}\), \(B=\frac{2}{5}\) and \(C=\frac{1}{5}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{3}{5(x+2)} + \frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2x+1}{x^2+1}\right)\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\int \frac{dx}{x+2} + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{x^2+1}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\log|x+2| + \frac{1}{5}\log|x^2+1| + \frac{1}{5}\tan^{-1}x + C\).

stem: Integrate the rational function \(\frac{1}{x(x^n+1)}\). [Hint: multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^{n-1}\) and put \(x^n=t\)]
Integrate the rational function \(\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)(2-\sin x)}\). [Hint: Put \(\sin x=t\)]

solution: Put \(f(x) = x\) (first function) and \(g(x) = \cos x\) (second function). Then, integration by parts gives \(\int x \cos x \, dx = x \int \cos x \, dx - \int [\frac{d}{dx}(x) \int \cos x \, dx]\, dx = x \sin x - \int \sin x \, dx = x \sin x + \cos x + C\). Note the choice of first and second function matters: taking \(f(x) = \cos x\) and \(g(x) = x\) instead reduces the integral to the more complicated \(\int \sin x \, \frac{x^2}{2}\, dx\).

We cannot guess a function whose derivative is \(\log x\). Take \(\log x\) as the first function and the constant function \(1\) as the second function; the integral of the second function is \(x\). Hence \(\int (\log x \cdot 1)\, dx = \log x \int 1\, dx - \int [\frac{d}{dx}(\log x) \int 1\, dx]\, dx = (\log x)\cdot x - \int \frac{1}{x}\, x \, dx = x \log x - x + C\).

Take the first function as \(x\) and the second function as \(e^{x}\). The integral of the second function is \(e^{x}\). Therefore \(\int x\, e^{x} \, dx = x\, e^{x} - \int 1 \cdot e^{x} \, dx = x e^{x} - e^{x} + C\).

Let the first function be \(\sin^{-1} x\) and the second function be \(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\). First find the integral of the second function \(\int \frac{x\, dx}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\): put \(t = 1 - x^{2}\), then \(dt = -2x\, dx\), so \(\int \frac{x\, dx}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} = -\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = -\sqrt{t} = -\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\). Hence \(\int \frac{x \sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\, dx = (\sin^{-1} x)(-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}) - \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}(-\sqrt{1-x^{2}})\, dx = -\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1} x + x + C = x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1} x + C\). (Alternatively, substitute \(\sin^{-1} x = \theta\) and then integrate by parts.)

Take \(e^{x}\) as the first function and \(\sin x\) as the second function. Integrating by parts, \(I = \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx = e^{x}(-\cos x) + \int e^{x} \cos x \, dx = -e^{x}\cos x + I_1\) (say) ...(1). Taking \(e^{x}\) and \(\cos x\) as the first and second functions in \(I_1\), we get \(I_1 = e^{x} \sin x - \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx\). Substituting \(I_1\) in (1): \(I = -e^{x}\cos x + e^{x}\sin x - I\), or \(2I = e^{x}(\sin x - \cos x)\). Hence \(I = \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx = \frac{e^{x}}{2}(\sin x - \cos x) + C\).

We have \(I = \int e^{x}\left(\tan^{-1} x + \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right) dx\). Consider \(f(x) = \tan^{-1} x\), then \(f'(x) = \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\). Thus the integrand is of the form \(e^{x}[f(x) + f'(x)]\), and \(\int e^{x}[f(x)+f'(x)]\, dx = e^{x} f(x) + C\). Therefore \(I = e^{x} \tan^{-1} x + C\).

We have \(I = \int \frac{(x^{2}+1)\, e^{x}}{(x+1)^{2}}\, dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x^{2}-1+1+1}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x^{2}-1}{(x+1)^{2}} + \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x-1}{x+1} + \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx\). Consider \(f(x) = \frac{x-1}{x+1}\), then \(f'(x) = \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\). Thus the integrand is of the form \(e^{x}[f(x) + f'(x)]\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^{2}+1}{(x+1)^{2}}\, e^{x} \, dx = \frac{x-1}{x+1}\, e^{x} + C\).

Note that \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,dx = \int \sqrt{(x+1)^2 + 4}\,dx\). Put \(x + 1 = y\), so that \(dx = dy\). Then \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,dx = \int \sqrt{y^2 + 2^2}\,dy = \frac{1}{2}\,y\sqrt{y^2 + 4} + \frac{4}{2}\log\left|\,y + \sqrt{y^2 + 4}\,\right| + C\) [using 7.6.2 (ii)] \(= \frac{1}{2}(x+1)\sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5} + 2\log\left|\,x + 1 + \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,\right| + C\).

Note that \(\int \sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2}\,dx = \int \sqrt{4 - (x+1)^2}\,dx\). Put \(x + 1 = y\) so that \(dx = dy\). Thus \(\int \sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2}\,dx = \int \sqrt{4 - y^2}\,dy = \frac{1}{2}\,y\sqrt{4 - y^2} + \frac{4}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{y}{2} + C\) [using 7.6.2 (iii)] \(= \frac{1}{2}(x+1)\sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x+1}{2}\right) + C\).

subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem
solution: Let \(I = \int_{2}^{3} x^{2}\,dx\). Since \(\int x^{2}\,dx = \frac{x^{3}}{3} = F(x)\), therefore, by the second fundamental theorem, we get \(I = F(3) - F(2) = \frac{27}{3} - \frac{8}{3} = \frac{19}{3}\).

subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem
solution: Let \(I = \int_{4}^{9} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\left(30 - x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)^{2}}\,dx\). We first find the anti derivative of the integrand. Put \(30 - x^{\frac{3}{2}} = t\). Then \(-\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}\,dx = dt\) or \(\sqrt{x}\,dx = -\frac{2}{3}\,dt\). Thus, \(\int \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\left(30 - x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)^{2}}\,dx = -\frac{2}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t^{2}} = \frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{t}\right] = \frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{30 - x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right] = F(x)\). Therefore, by the second fundamental theorem of calculus, we have \(I = F(9) - F(4) = \frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{30 - x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right]_{4}^{9} = \frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{(30 - 27)} - \frac{1}{30 - 8}\right] = \frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{22}\right] = \frac{19}{99}\).

subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem
solution: Let \(I = \int_{1}^{2} \frac{x\,dx}{(x+1)(x+2)}\). Using partial fraction, we get \(\frac{x}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{-1}{x+1} + \frac{2}{x+2}\). So \(\int \frac{x\,dx}{(x+1)(x+2)} = -\log|x+1| + 2\log|x+2| = F(x)\). Therefore, by the second fundamental theorem of calculus, we have \(I = F(2) - F(1) = [-\log 3 + 2\log 4] - [-\log 2 + 2\log 3] = -3\log 3 + \log 2 + 2\log 4 = \log\left(\frac{32}{27}\right)\).

subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem
solution: Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin^{3} 2t \cos 2t \,dt\). Consider \(\int \sin^{3} 2t \cos 2t \,dt\). Put \(\sin 2t = u\) so that \(2\cos 2t\,dt = du\) or \(\cos 2t\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\,du\). So \(\int \sin^{3} 2t \cos 2t \,dt = \frac{1}{2}\int u^{3}\,du = \frac{1}{8}[u^{4}] = \frac{1}{8}\sin^{4} 2t = F(t)\) say. Therefore, by the second fundamental theorem of integral calculus, \(I = F\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) - F(0) = \frac{1}{8}\left[\sin^{4}\frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{4} 0\right] = \frac{1}{8}\).

solution: Let \(t = \tan^{-1} x\), then \(dt = \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\,dx\). The new limits are, when \(x=0\), \(t=0\) and when \(x=1\), \(t=\frac{\pi}{4}\). Thus, as \(x\) varies from 0 to 1, \(t\) varies from 0 to \(\frac{\pi}{4}\). Therefore \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\tan^{-1} x}{1+x^{2}}\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} t\,dt = \left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/4} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\pi^{2}}{16} - 0\right] = \frac{\pi^{2}}{32}\).

stem: Evaluate the integral using substitution: \(\int_{0}^{2} x\sqrt{x+2}\,dx\) (Put \(x+2 = t^{2}\)).
Evaluate the integral using substitution: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^{2} x}\,dx\).
Evaluate the integral using substitution: \(\int_{1}^{2} \left(\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{2x^{2}}\right) e^{2x}\,dx\).
The value of the integral \(\int_{1/3}^{1} \frac{(x-x^{3})^{1/3}}{x^{4}}\,dx\) is

solution: Put \(t = 1 + \sin 6x\), so that \(dt = 6\cos 6x\, dx\). Therefore \(\int \cos 6x\sqrt{1+\sin 6x}\, dx = \frac{1}{6}\int t^{\frac{1}{2}}\, dt = \frac{1}{6}\times\frac{2}{3}(t)^{\frac{3}{2}} + C = \frac{1}{9}(1+\sin 6x)^{\frac{3}{2}} + C\).

We have \(\int \frac{(x^4 - x)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^5}\, dx = \int \frac{\left(1 - \frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^4}\, dx\). Put \(1 - \frac{1}{x^3} = 1 - x^{-3} = t\), so that \(\frac{3}{x^4}\, dx = dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{(x^4 - x)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^5}\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\int t^{\frac{1}{4}}\, dt = \frac{1}{3}\times\frac{4}{5} t^{\frac{5}{4}} + C = \frac{4}{15}\left(1 - \frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{\frac{5}{4}} + C\).

By division, \(\frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = (x+1) + \frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\). Now express \(\frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}\). So \(1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x-1)\). Equating coefficients gives \(A + B = 0,\; C - B = 0,\; A - C = 1\), which give \(A = \frac{1}{2},\; B = C = -\frac{1}{2}\). Hence \(\frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = \frac{1}{2(x-1)} - \frac{1}{2}\frac{x}{x^2+1} - \frac{1}{2(x^2+1)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\, dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + x + \frac{1}{2}\log|x-1| - \frac{1}{4}\log(x^2+1) - \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x + C\).
_note: The book prints the denominator as (x-1)(x^2+x+1) in the intermediate 'substituting (3) in (1)' and 'Therefore' lines; the correct denominator per the example statement is (x-1)(x^2+1) — used here.

solution: Let \(I = \int \left[\log(\log x) + \frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\right] dx = \int \log(\log x)\, dx + \int \frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\, dx\). In the first integral, take 1 as the second function and integrate by parts: \(I = x\log(\log x) - \int \frac{1}{x\log x} x\, dx + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} = x\log(\log x) - \int \frac{dx}{\log x} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2}\) ... (1). Again, consider \(\int \frac{dx}{\log x}\), take 1 as the second function and integrate by parts: \(\int \frac{dx}{\log x} = \frac{x}{\log x} - \int x\left\{-\frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\cdot\frac{1}{x}\right\} dx = \frac{x}{\log x} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2}\) ... (2). Putting (2) in (1), \(I = x\log(\log x) - \frac{x}{\log x} - \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} = x\log(\log x) - \frac{x}{\log x} + C\).

We have \(I = \int \left[\sqrt{\cot x} + \sqrt{\tan x}\right] dx = \int \sqrt{\tan x}\,(1 + \cot x)\, dx\). Put \(\tan x = t^2\), so that \(\sec^2 x\, dx = 2t\, dt\), or \(dx = \frac{2t\, dt}{1+t^4}\). Then \(I = \int t\left(1 + \frac{1}{t^2}\right)\frac{2t}{1+t^4}\, dt = 2\int \frac{t^2+1}{t^4+1}\, dt = 2\int \frac{\left(1+\frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt}{\left(t - \frac{1}{t}\right)^2 + 2}\). Put \(t - \frac{1}{t} = y\), so that \(\left(1 + \frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt = dy\). Then \(I = 2\int \frac{dy}{y^2 + (\sqrt 2)^2} = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\frac{y}{\sqrt 2} + C = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{t^2-1}{\sqrt 2\, t}\right) + C = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan x - 1}{\sqrt{2\tan x}}\right) + C\).

Let \(I = \int \frac{\sin 2x \cos 2x}{\sqrt{9 - \cos^4 2x}}\, dx\). Put \(\cos^2(2x) = t\) so that \(4\sin 2x \cos 2x\, dx = -dt\). Therefore \(I = -\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{9 - t^2}} = -\frac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{t}{3}\right) + C = -\frac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}\left[\frac{1}{3}\cos^2 2x\right] + C\).

subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem
solution: Here \(f(x) = |x\sin\pi x| = \begin{cases} x\sin\pi x & \text{for } -1 \le x \le 1 \\ -x\sin\pi x & \text{for } 1 \le x \le \frac{3}{2} \end{cases}\). Therefore \(\int_{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}} |x\sin\pi x|\, dx = \int_{-1}^{1} x\sin\pi x\, dx + \int_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} -x\sin\pi x\, dx = \int_{-1}^{1} x\sin\pi x\, dx - \int_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} x\sin\pi x\, dx\). Integrating by parts, \(\int_{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}} |x\sin\pi x|\, dx = \left[\frac{-x\cos\pi x}{\pi} + \frac{\sin\pi x}{\pi^2}\right]_{-1}^{1} - \left[\frac{-x\cos\pi x}{\pi} + \frac{\sin\pi x}{\pi^2}\right]_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} = \frac{2}{\pi} - \left[-\frac{1}{\pi^2} - \frac{1}{\pi}\right] = \frac{3}{\pi} + \frac{1}{\pi^2}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{x\, dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{(\pi - x)\, dx}{a^2\cos^2(\pi-x) + b^2\sin^2(\pi-x)}\) (using \(P_4\)) \(= \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} - I\). Thus \(2I = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x}\), or \(I = \frac{\pi}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} = \frac{\pi}{2}\cdot 2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x}\) (using \(P_6\)) \(= \pi\left[\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\frac{\sec^2 x\, dx}{a^2 + b^2\tan^2 x} + \int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\csc^2 x\, dx}{a^2\cot^2 x + b^2}\right]\). Putting \(\tan x = t\) and \(\cot x = u\), \(I = \pi\left[\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dt}{a^2 + b^2 t^2} - \int_{1}^{0}\frac{du}{a^2 u^2 + b^2}\right] = \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{bt}{a}\right]_{0}^{1} - \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{au}{b}\right]_{1}^{0} = \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{b}{a} + \tan^{-1}\frac{a}{b}\right] = \frac{\pi^2}{2ab}\).
